evidence_packet.evidence_text: Domestic abuse prevention orders a 'step in right direction' - BBC News Image caption, Jill Caldwell, who is chief executive of domestic abuse charity Endeavour, welcomed the new orders By Mairead Smyth , North West and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 1 hour ago A charity has welcomed the rollout of domestic abuse protection orders (DAPOs) across England and Wales but warned more needs to be done to protect and support victims. Under new restrictions, abusers could be forced to hand over house keys, social media passwords, phones and laptops in a bid to protect victims. Jill Caldwell, chief executive of Bolton-based domestic abuse charity Endeavour, said the rollout was "a really good start" but the government needed to ensure the orders were effectively enforced by police and specialist support services were in place for victims. Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, said the government was " rolling out the strongest protections ever available to victims". , external "This government is taking action and will always stand with victims and survivors of domestic abuse," she said. A DAPO can be made by a court to protect victims from all forms of domestic abuse, including non-physical abuse and controlling or coercive behaviour. Applications can also be made by the police, the victim or someone who is not directly involved, known as a third party - such as family member, a friend, or a social worker. Those who breach the order could be charged with a criminal offence, punishable by up to five years in prison. Unlike previous protections, DAPOs can remain in place for as long as necessary in a bid to keep victims safe. In a statement on Tuesday evening, Co-op Live said it was conducting a "full review" into the incident. "The safety and security of our guests, artists and staff remain our highest priority, and we take that responsibility extremely seriously." The 32-year-old footballer, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan this summer , is alleged to have driven his £150,000 Range Rover at 58mph (93km/h) in a 50mph zone on the M60 in March 2026. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Stones did not respond to two letters and on 27 April was charged with failing to furnish driver information. He has since pleaded not guilty. Stones is represented by Freeman & Co Solicitors, a law firm whose owner Nick Freeman has advised several celebrity clients in motoring cases and has trademarked his nickname of Mr Loophole. Stones now faces trial on 29 September 2028 at Warrington Magistrates' Court. He has denied receiving the request for information from the police and asked prosecutors to prove it was served. In a letter to the court, Stones's lawyers added: "It was not reasonably practicable for the defendant to give the information within the requisite period." They also claimed GMP included "hearsay" in its single justice procedure notice dated 20 October 2026. Stones's team requested that the trial should last at least two hours and be heard in the morning. They also asked for permission for him to be excused from a pre-trial case management hearing were one to be required. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Memorial plaques and urns worth £20k stolen from Stockport cemetery - BBC News Image caption, Police said the theft took place between 17:30 on Sunday and 05:30 on Monday By Georgie Docker and Richard Stead , North West Published 24 November 2026 Memorial plaques and grave ornaments worth more than £20,000 have been stolen from a cemetery in Stockport. A volunteer at St Mark's Church in Bredbury discovered about 94 cast-iron memorial plaques and 80 stone and granite flower urns had been stolen at about 05:30 GMT on Monday. Greater Manchester Police said the total estimated value of the stolen items is in excess of £20,000, adding "this figure may increase as further families visit the churchyard and report additional missing items". "You just can't believe it," Reverend Andy Bull said. "For the plaques to have disappeared - the sentimental value of that is huge to people." Image caption, Reverend Andy Bull said it was 'hard to comprehend' that someone would steal memorial plaques and urns Police estimated the memorial plaques were worth more than £8,000 and the stone and granite urns more than £12,000. But Bull said the loss to families was far greater. "People have a very strong affiliation with the graveyard. It's a place where they come to remember loved ones," he said. "A lot of people are feeling very sad that a place which was there to remember loved ones has become fraught with emotions." GMP said it was reviewing CCTV footage to identify any people or vehicles in the area during the period of the theft. Jamie, 17, was seriously injured in Benidorm on 10 November and has had two emergency operations. His family, from Bury in Greater Manchester, said doctors had been reducing Jamie's sedation and went on to say that he had responded to their voices and had followed instructions. While the teenager's lungs are improving, he remains seriously ill, still requires support from a ventilator and faces further surgery, they said. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A charity has welcomed the rollout of domestic abuse protection orders (DAPOs) across England and Wales but warned more needs to be done to protect and support victims Under new restrictions, abusers could be forced to hand over house keys, social media passwords, phones and laptops in a bid to protect victims Jill Caldwell, chief executive of Bolton-based domestic abuse charity Endeavour, said the rollout was "a really good start" but the government needed to ensure the orders were effectively enforced by police and specialist support services were in place for victims Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, said the government was " rolling out the strongest protections ever available to victims". , external "This government is taking action and will always stand with victims and survivors of domestic abuse," she said A DAPO can be made by a court to protect victims from all forms of domestic abuse, including non-physical abuse and controlling or coercive behaviour

evidence_packet.evidence_text: England defender John Stones faces trial in 2028 over an allegation he failed to provide driver information to police The 32-year-old footballer, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan this summer , is alleged to have driven his £150,000 Range Rover at 58mph (93km/h) in a 50mph zone on the M60 in March 2026 Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Stones did not respond to two letters and on 27 April was charged with failing to furnish driver information. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A council's adult social care services have again been rated as requiring improvement by inspectors, as the authority presses ahead with plans that could see up to 100 jobs cut The Care Quality Commission (CQC) said people's experiences of adult social care provision at Warrington Council were "mixed", but found signs of progress in safeguarding following criticism of the service last year The report comes as the council looks to save about £34m from adult social care as part of wider plans to reduce debt The CQC said there were "early indications" that safeguarding practice had improved following the introduction of a new safeguarding hub Last year, the CQC said the council's safeguarding system "didn't structurally work" . However, inspectors said it was still "too early to tell" whether recent changes would deliver lasting improvements The CQC said council leaders had shown "a real commitment to making improvements"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The co-founder of a restaurant has been banned from acting as a company director for five years after his company failed to account for over £363,000 in furlough payments during the coronavirus pandemic, the Insolvency Service said Patrick Hall, 45, helped establish The Laundrette in Chorlton, Manchester, which closed in 2025 after 12 years in business, citing "rising costs and insufficient government support" The Insolvency Service said Winchester Services Limited, which ran the restaurant, repeatedly failed to provide evidence that it was entitled to the payments Hall, from Levenshulme, agreed to a disqualification undertaking and a five-year ban The restaurant and bar, known for its pizzas and cocktails, opened on Beech Road in 2013 and was run through several companies under Hall's directorship Winchester Services Limited received the furlough payments between April 2020 and May 2021

evidence_packet.summary: Memorial plaques and grave ornaments worth more than £20,000 have been stolen from a cemetery in Stockport A volunteer at St Mark's Church in Bredbury discovered about 94 cast-iron memorial plaques and 80 stone and granite flower urns had been stolen at about 05:30 GMT on Monday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Memorial plaques and grave ornaments worth more than £20,000 have been stolen from a cemetery in Stockport A volunteer at St Mark's Church in Bredbury discovered about 94 cast-iron memorial plaques and 80 stone and granite flower urns had been stolen at about 05:30 GMT on Monday Greater Manchester Police said the total estimated value of the stolen items is in excess of £20,000, adding "this figure may increase as further families visit the churchyard and report additional missing items" "You just can't believe it," Reverend Andy Bull said. "For the plaques to have disappeared - the sentimental value of that is huge to people." Police estimated the memorial plaques were worth more than £8,000 and the stone and granite urns more than £12,000 But Bull said the loss to families was far greater

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A head teacher has said he would support his school joining a scheme designed to ban most cars from parking around it during peak times Steven Worthington, who runs the Dean Trust Ardwick in east Manchester, said there had been "a number of incidents" and "our young people are subjected to bad traffic pollution" He told the BBC that "traffic is very congested during school drop-off and pick-up times... we're keen to address this'' Greater Manchester's School Streets initiative - which also encourages children to walk, cycle or scoot - was launched five years ago and now covers 51 schools and more than 20,000 pupils By 2030, Transport for Greater Manchester wants 70% of primary school pupils to walk, wheel, scoot or cycle to and from school Roads surrounding the Dean Trust Academy are chaotic at peak times, with motorists often parking on double yellow lines or leaving their engines running while waiting for their children to finish school

evidence_packet.summary: A teenager who fell from a sixth-floor hotel balcony in Spain has opened his eyes and responded to his relatives after spending nearly two weeks in intensive care, his family has said Jamie, 17, was seriously injured in Benidorm on 10 November and has had two emergency operations
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A teenager who fell from a sixth-floor hotel balcony in Spain has opened his eyes and responded to his relatives after spending nearly two weeks in intensive care, his family has said Jamie, 17, was seriously injured in Benidorm on 10 November and has had two emergency operations His family, from Bury in Greater Manchester, said doctors had been reducing Jamie's sedation and went on to say that he had responded to their voices and had followed instructions While the teenager's lungs are improving, he remains seriously ill, still requires support from a ventilator and faces further surgery, they said "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions," the family said "After nearly two weeks of worry, waiting and uncertainty, those moments meant more to us than we could ever put into words."

evidence_packet.title: Man's shock at Ryanair flight to Spain using wife's passport
evidence_packet.lead: A man who mistakenly travelled to Spain using his wife's passport has said he is still baffled about how he was able to make the trip without being stopped in the UK Ben Moore, from Talke, in Staffordshire, noticed there was a problem soon after getting off his Ryanair flight whi
evidence_packet.summary: A man who mistakenly travelled to Spain using his wife's passport has said he is still baffled about how he was able to make the trip without being stopped in the UK Ben Moore, from Talke, in Staffordshire, noticed there was a problem soon after getting off his Ryanair flight whi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who mistakenly travelled to Spain using his wife's passport has said he is still baffled about how he was able to make the trip without being stopped in the UK Ben Moore, from Talke, in Staffordshire, noticed there was a problem soon after getting off his Ryanair flight while he was queuing to get his passport checked at Alicante airport "I opened up the passport there and, to my horror, it was my wife's photo on the passport," he said. "The lads who I was with basically said the colour drained out of me immediately." Third-party provider Swissport, which carries out Ryanair's checks at Manchester Airport where Moore flew from, said it was now reinforcing mandatory boarding procedures Moore, who was travelling to Alicante on a stag party with friends, told BBC Radio Stoke he initially thought he must have picked up his wife's passport in addition to his own He said he approached Spanish police who - along with the language barrier - appeared to be as confused as he was about how he had turned up there without his own passport

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts A couple in court and their phone that received 1,861 calls in two weeks Carl Lomas was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested - but he did it anyway Both defendants were homeles Add to preferred sources Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 05:55, 25 Nov 2026 Updated 06:10, 25 Nov 2026 A drug dealer who 'simply continued to peddle heroin and crack cocaine' following his arrest has found himself hauled before the courts alongside his girlfriend Carl Lomas and Sarah Warburton were both found with heroin and crack cocaine after officers swooped in Stockport . A ‘burner’ phone used to supply drugs received 1,861 incoming calls within a two week period before it was seized in July The pair, who were both remanded in prison, were sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester yesterday (November 24). Lomas was jailed while Warburton was handed a suspended prison sentence Prosecuting, Andy Evans said that an officer was on patrol in Heaton Norris on November 19 last year when Lomas emerged from a house said to have been linked to drug dealing The officer stopped Lomas, who was found to be in possession of 11.1g of heroin and 6.88g of crack cocaine. He also had a Nokia ‘burner’ phone and £213 in cash. He was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Major health update after Bury boy, 17, fell 60ft from Benidorm hotel balcony Jamie, from Bury, has suffered extensive injuries but made a big step forward in his recovery on Sunday as his family raise money to get him home Add to preferred sourc A teenager from Bury who fell 60ft from a Benidorm hotel balcony has opened his eyes and responded to his loved ones two weeks after the incident. Jamie, 17, was on holiday with his mum, Gemma, 36, and her friends for Fiesta Week when he fell from the sixth floor his hotel, the s The teen underwent two emergency operations in Alicante and was heavily sedated after he suffered extensive injuries. Jamie fractured both sides of his chest, punctured a lung, ruptured an artery, and broke bones in his pelvis, both legs and one arm on November 10 His family said Jamie opened his eyes on Sunday (November 22) and followed instructions after doctors reduced his sedation. Despite his progress, Jamie remains seriously ill and continues to require support from a ventilator, The Mirror reports His family said: "Over the last few days, Jamie has started showing some encouraging signs of improvement. His lungs are looking better, the amount of oxygen he's needing has reduced, and the doctors have been gradually trying to bring him out of sedation "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions. After nearly two weeks of worry, waiting and uncertainty, those moments meant more to us than we could ever put in

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham vows to scrap NDAs for victims of sexual abuse and grooming Burnham says he wants the changes to make sure 'victims can speak out about their own abuse.' Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 22:32, 24 N The Prime Minister has announced a string on limits on NDAs aimed at preventing them from being used to silence sexual abuse victims Andy Burnham has brought forward amendments to NDAs which will come in effect in January. The changes come after a series of campaigns led by the likes of Zelda Perkins The new rules will limit NDAS, meaning victims of crime will not be restricted on who they can speak to, even if they sign one. The list of confidants could include police, family, friends, victims’ services or even the media if they choose The Prime Minister is drawing a line in the sand on victims being silenced to protect perpetrators, announcing strict limits on when NDAs can be used NDAs between a worker and their employer will have relevant confidentiality clauses automatically voided if they experience or see harassment at work

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'Truth has its own power': The Rochdale veteran whose decades-long fight for justice may soon be over John Morris was one of thousands of young men posted to Christmas Island as part of Operation Grapple, Britain’s campaign to build and test A nuclear test veteran from Rochdale who has spent decades fighting for answers following the death of his baby son says he hopes he will live long enough to see justice finally delivered John Morris, 89, has welcomed the announcement of an independent panel into the impact of Britain's nuclear weapons testing, describing it as a breakthrough after what he believes has been a cover-up of several decades The panel, announced by Prime Minister Andy Burnham , will be chaired by Bishop James Jones and investigate the potential impact of nuclear testing on veterans and their families It will follow the model of the Hillsborough Independent Panel, also chaired by Bishop Jones, with the aim of delivering an interim report in time for the 75th anniversary of Britain's first nuclear weapons test For John, who witnessed four nuclear explosions in 1957, the announcement represents a significant moment in a campaign that has spanned much of his life

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan A link road across Wigan has been planned for 77 years – is it finally about to be built? The 2.5km new Wigan to Hindley road would be part of an east to west route which eventually hopes to link the M6 and M61 Add to preferred sources Comments An initial consultation on the long-planned Wigan to Hindley link road (WHLR) ends this week with hopes that building it will begin in 2029. The project, previously known as the East-West Link Road or the A5225 has been an aspiration since 1949 The single carriageway road would be 2.5 kilometres long and would take traffic from the A49 Westwood Way to the A5777 Manchester Road and would include links with Warrington Road, Phoenix Way, Seaman Way and south to Liverpool Road Over the decades, efforts have been made to secure funding to progress the scheme In October 2023, the Department for Transport published ‘Network North’ – a £36 billion plan to improve transport in the north of England In March, the government committed £153m to the scheme which was first called for shortly after the Second World War

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Co-Op Live 'Tests ongoing' to identify substance that sparked Don Toliver Co-op Live concert evacuation Manchester council leader Garry Bridges said it remained a 'devleoping incident' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 14:05, 24 N Tests are ongoing to identify an unknown substance that sparked the evacuation of Co-op Live during a gig by US rapper Don Toliver , Manchester council's leader has said. More than 12,000 people were inside the venue as a major incident was declared on Sunday night One person was taken to hospital and 89 concert-goers were treated at the scene . Police initially said tear gas was thought to have been released inside the arena , but later described it as an 'unknown substance' Mobile phone video footage showed concert-goers struggling to breathe and coughing as they walked out of the venue. In a statement today, Manchester council leader Garry Bridges said it remained a 'developing incident' He told Sky News: "Tests are still ongoing to determine the nature of the substance that was released. This is a developing incident and we, alongside our partners, are working to establish the facts of what took place on Sunday evening." Coun Bridges also thanked emergency services, and urged any concert-goer who experiences adverse symptoms to contact their GP, ring 111 or go to hospital

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Historic £1.4m Salford church with 4am party licence up for sale - and the extraordinary story of the street around it Built in 1819 in a post-Napoleonic surge of religious fervour - and later rocked by a minister's mysterious scandal - the Gr Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:23, 24 Nov 2026 An empty Georgian church may be on the brink of salvation. The former Hope United Reformed Church in Chapel Street, Salford , dates from 1819 Close to Manchester city centre and less than 100 yards from Salford Central railway station it ceased to be a regular place of worship several years ago. Grade II listed, it is now up for sale for offers in excess of £1.4m Its roots lie in a surge of "Christian fervour" across the country at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. It sprang from a dearth of places to hear the Gospel in the rapidly industrialising Salford. It survived as a church through name changes, and the resignation of its first leader A dwindling congregation eventually meant a final Sunday Service was held in 2019. In 2023 plans to convert it into a complex of flats, a community centre and commercial use were submitted to the City Council Hope United Reformed Church on Chapel St, Salford, pictured today. It is up for sale for £1.4m. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Here' Add to preferred sources Comments News Liv Clarke Tourism writer 06:22, 24 Nov 2026 Updated 07:37, 25 Nov 2026 On May 21, 2025 I boarded a flight from Manchester Airport, just like hundreds of other passengers that day. Except my flight was rather unusual I was among the exclusive group of passengers to fly on Global Airlines’ flight from Manchester Airport to New York JFK that day, only a week after it had operated its inaugural flight from Glasgow to New York. As a ‘new’ airline operating an A380, there was certainly a buzz in t In many ways, the day played out like any exciting launch of a new route; passengers were given branded cupcakes at check-in and encouraged to pose next to sparkly photo point; aviation enthusiasts grabbed photos of the plane on the tarmac; and the CEO James Asquith himself board Yet in other ways, there were clues back then that the future of Global was a precarious one. Its website was incredibly basic, the plane interior was scruffy, and there was just the small matter that it didn’t even have its own operating licence Passengers board the Global flight from Manchester Airport to New York JFK on Wednesday, May 21, 2025 (Image: Liv Clarke)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts A couple in court and their phone that received 1,861 calls in two weeks Carl Lomas was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested - but he did it anyway Both defendants were homeles Add to preferred sources Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 05:55, 25 Nov 2026 Updated 06:10, 25 Nov 2026 A drug dealer who 'simply continued to peddle heroin and crack cocaine' following his arrest has found himself hauled before the courts alongside his girlfriend Carl Lomas and Sarah Warburton were both found with heroin and crack cocaine after officers swooped in Stockport . A ‘burner’ phone used to supply drugs received 1,861 incoming calls within a two week period before it was seized in July The pair, who were both remanded in prison, were sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester yesterday (November 24). Lomas was jailed while Warburton was handed a suspended prison sentence Prosecuting, Andy Evans said that an officer was on patrol in Heaton Norris on November 19 last year when Lomas emerged from a house said to have been linked to drug dealing The officer stopped Lomas, who was found to be in possession of 11.1g of heroin and 6.88g of crack cocaine. He also had a Nokia ‘burner’ phone and £213 in cash. He was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Major health update after Bury boy, 17, fell 60ft from Benidorm hotel balcony Jamie, from Bury, has suffered extensive injuries but made a big step forward in his recovery on Sunday as his family raise money to get him home Add to preferred sourc A teenager from Bury who fell 60ft from a Benidorm hotel balcony has opened his eyes and responded to his loved ones two weeks after the incident. Jamie, 17, was on holiday with his mum, Gemma, 36, and her friends for Fiesta Week when he fell from the sixth floor his hotel, the s The teen underwent two emergency operations in Alicante and was heavily sedated after he suffered extensive injuries. Jamie fractured both sides of his chest, punctured a lung, ruptured an artery, and broke bones in his pelvis, both legs and one arm on November 10 His family said Jamie opened his eyes on Sunday (November 22) and followed instructions after doctors reduced his sedation. Despite his progress, Jamie remains seriously ill and continues to require support from a ventilator, The Mirror reports His family said: "Over the last few days, Jamie has started showing some encouraging signs of improvement. His lungs are looking better, the amount of oxygen he's needing has reduced, and the doctors have been gradually trying to bring him out of sedation "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions. Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 22:32, 24 N The Prime Minister has announced a string on limits on NDAs aimed at preventing them from being used to silence sexual abuse victims Andy Burnham has brought forward amendments to NDAs which will come in effect in January. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Historic £1.4m Salford church with 4am party licence up for sale - and the extraordinary story of the street around it Built in 1819 in a post-Napoleonic surge of religious fervour - and later rocked by a minister's mysterious scandal - the Gr Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:23, 24 Nov 2026 An empty Georgian church may be on the brink of salvation. The former Hope United Reformed Church in Chapel Street, Salford , dates from 1819 Close to Manchester city centre and less than 100 yards from Salford Central railway station it ceased to be a regular place of worship several years ago. Grade II listed, it is now up for sale for offers in excess of £1.4m Its roots lie in a surge of "Christian fervour" across the country at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. It sprang from a dearth of places to hear the Gospel in the rapidly industrialising Salford. It survived as a church through name changes, and the resignation of its first leader A dwindling congregation eventually meant a final Sunday Service was held in 2019. In 2023 plans to convert it into a complex of flats, a community centre and commercial use were submitted to the City Council Hope United Reformed Church on Chapel St, Salford, pictured today. evidence_packet.title: Substance at Don Toliver Manchester show may be linked to robberies, police say
evidence_packet.lead: More than 12,000 people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday One person was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood"
evidence_packet.summary: More than 12,000 people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday One person was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: More than 12,000 people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday One person was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood" Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said officers received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert but no arrests had been made and the substance had not yet been identified Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said there was "no wider ongoing risk" to the public "We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending," he said In a statement on Tuesday evening, Co-op Live said it was conducting a "full review" into the incident

title: Stockport: Drug rape husband wanted 'extra fun', court told

evidence_packet.title: Stockport: Drug rape husband wanted 'extra fun', court told
evidence_packet.lead: A man who drugged and raped his wife for more than 20 years advertised online "looking for some extra fun and games", a court heard The victim's husband pleaded guilty earlier this year to multiple offences dating from 2004, including rape, sexual assault and administering a subs
evidence_packet.summary: A man who drugged and raped his wife for more than 20 years advertised online "looking for some extra fun and games", a court heard The victim's husband pleaded guilty earlier this year to multiple offences dating from 2004, including rape, sexual assault and administering a subs
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who drugged and raped his wife for more than 20 years advertised online "looking for some extra fun and games", a court heard The victim's husband pleaded guilty earlier this year to multiple offences dating from 2004, including rape, sexual assault and administering a substance with intent to commit a sexual offence The man in his 60s, who cannot be identified to protect his wife's anonymity, took images and videos of his offending as she lay "out of it" on their bed, and then shared them online From 2023 onwards at the latest, the prosecution says he began inviting other men to their home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, where it is said they too sexually abused her He will give evidence later this week against nine men on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court over their alleged roles in the offending Several of the defendants initially met the husband through Fabswingers.com, a website for those interested in swinging, before they moved contact to different messaging apps

evidence_packet.title: Two men admit sex offences against Stockport woman drugged and raped by husband
evidence_packet.lead: Two men have pleaded guilty to sexual offences against a woman who was drugged and raped by her husband without her knowledge Robert Stewart, 70, from Stockport admitted rape and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court In a separ
evidence_packet.summary: Two men have pleaded guilty to sexual offences against a woman who was drugged and raped by her husband without her knowledge Robert Stewart, 70, from Stockport admitted rape and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court In a separ
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two men have pleaded guilty to sexual offences against a woman who was drugged and raped by her husband without her knowledge Robert Stewart, 70, from Stockport admitted rape and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court In a separate hearing at Manchester Magistrates' Court, Tommy Golden, 59, pleaded guilty to sexual assault involving the same woman in June 2025 Golden appeared via video link from HMP Risley, where he is serving a prison sentence District Judge Simon Blakebrough said his offending was too serious to be dealt with by magistrates. His case was sent to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court, where he is due to appear in December During the hearing, Golden said that he had not spoken to a solicitor before entering a guilty plea

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

In August, Nothing Gold Can Stay took Robert Frost’s poem about transience as its starting point. Where that show dwelt on things passing, this one is more interested in what lasts The four contributing artists each approach time differently, thinking about how the past and the future shape the way ideas are understood. Anna Clough, a Cumbrian-born artist based at Salford’s Paradise Works, has made walking performances tracing mining landscapes from the Neo Sheffield’s Charlotte Dawson treats everyday objects – souvenirs, collections – as vessels for memory. Olivia England, who graduated from Manchester School of Art alongside Clough, reworks found objects, text and imagery through bookbinding and print, while London-based Elliot Fo Seeing the work from a perspective that isn’t your own is meant to open up conversations about the legacy of ideas, collective memory and what our actions leave behind for people we’ll never meet

title: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw

evidence_packet.title: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw
evidence_packet.lead: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw
evidence_packet.summary: Rasmus Højlund grabbed the opener for the visitors after 55 minutes, latching onto Billy Gilmour’s pass before drilling into the net. Enzo Maresca’s men reacted well to the setback and levelled 12 minutes later thanks to a thunderous left-footed strike from midfield maestro Ayyou
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rasmus Højlund grabbed the opener for the visitors after 55 minutes, latching onto Billy Gilmour’s pass before drilling into the net. Enzo Maresca’s men reacted well to the setback and levelled 12 minutes later thanks to a thunderous left-footed strike from midfield maestro Ayyoub Bouaddi, who claimed his first-ever goal in senior football. With City in the ascendancy, the visitors broke on a quick counter and restored their lead through Noa Lang’s controlled volley. But Maresca’s men showed grit and determination to fight back for a second time, with UEFA’s Player of the Match Cherki precisely finding the net with four minutes of normal time left at the Etihad to earn a point. Despite another sparkling individual performance, the Frenchman made it clear that the three points are always the utmost priority. “I don’t care about scoring my goal today. I want to win, just that,” said Cherki in an honest interview after the game. “Today we played good but we didn’t put a lot of energy I think. “We need to do more. We need to win this game, today I don’t care about scoring my goal, we need to win the game. We try to put all we have on the pitch. Sometimes the game is not like how you want. “Today it’s like the last two or three games. We need to work more and come back for a win. Just that.” The draw means we have three wins, one draw and one defeat in the competition this term, with three fixtures left of the League Phase. Attention now turns to Sunday’s huge Premier League clash away to league-leaders Arsenal and Cherki explained that City only have one intention heading into London. “We are in a difficult position, that is true because we didn’t win the game,” he continued. “We’re going to London to win the game. “Nothing more.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: John Stones John Stones faces trial in court after he's caught in £150,000 Range Rover on M60 Ex-Man City star John Stones will have to appear in court after he was seen on the M60 motorway Add to preferred sources News Press Association and Chris Sla Former Manchester City player John Stones has hired lawyers from a firm owned by 'Mr Loophole' to represent him as he faces trial The 32-year-old defender, who left City for Inter Milan in the summer, was caught driving his £150,000 Range Rover at 58mph through a 50mph zone of the M60 in March 2026 Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Mr Stones did not respond to two letters about his speeding. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC 'The stats are for us' - Enzo Maresca calm ahead of Man City trip to Arsenal Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca spoke about the confidence of his side heading into a Premier League game at Arsenal Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Simon B Enzo Maresca admitted he could not say anything to his Manchester City players after they 'fought to the end' against Napoli. The City boss was happy with the effort of his players, despite feeling they did not make the most of their chances and were made to pay by clinical oppon City were forced to come from behind twice in the Champions League game as their difficult run of form continues. It is now just one win in seven games, and they have conceded in 10 consecutive matches for the first time since 2019; in seven of those, their opponents have scored That has forced City to change their gameplan but they were their own worst enemy as they failed to break Napoli down in the first half and then more poor defensive play saw them concede. A trip to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday looks daunting, but Maresca is content "In this moment it's like this. The first 10 games we always scored first and then in this moment it is exactly the opposite way," he said. "We need to find a way to avoid that but I don't think that affects players in terms of confidence. When you go behind, you need to rush, so "Once again tonight on the ball all the numbers and stats are for us but the main thing is the balance between what we concede and what we create. We are always looking for three points, but we said many times that when you are not able to win it is important that you don't lose

title: Why Man City wore an orange kit vs Napoli in Champions League

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City are playing at home but are wearing orange instead of their home kit for the Champions League game with Napoli
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Why Man City wore an orange kit vs Napoli in Champions League Manchester City are playing at home but are wearing orange instead of their home kit for the Champions League game with Napoli Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Simon Bajkowski C Manchester City are taking on Napoli in the Champions League at the Etihad - but will not be wearing their blue home kit. The 2026/27 strip that was worn against Fulham on Saturday and is supposed to be used for every game where it doesn't clash is instead being benched for the v In its place is a limited edition orange kit that has been produced with both kit manufacturer Puma but also the club's 'official style fashionwear partner' CP Company. News of the kit was teased the day before the game and there was an orange display at Manchester Piccadilly tra The actual kit was kept firmly under wraps, although images did leak online through unofficial channels. City wore their fourth strip for the game with a bright orange shirt, shorts, and socks, with Napoli wearing their third 'euro jersey' kit City have worn limited edition kits for Champions League fixtures on two previous occasions, but are yet to win in one. They drew 0-0 with Inter in 2024 and lost 4-2 at Paris Saint-Germain in 2025 wearing a cream strip that drew inspiration from the Oasis album Definitely, Maybe Enzo Maresca's side need three points to keep their momentum in the competition going. They sit on nine points after four games and will likely need 16 from their remaining four to qualify directly for the last-16, with a trip to Barcelona up next in two weeks

evidence_packet.title: Premier League news: Moyes demands more from Grealish, Iraola wary of United threat
evidence_packet.lead: Everton’s playmaker returns after being stood down, while Liverpool’s head coach keeps focus for Anfield showdown
evidence_packet.summary: Everton’s playmaker returns after being stood down, while Liverpool’s head coach keeps focus for Anfield showdown
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Prefer the Guardian on Google 1. Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Mon “He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.” The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence. Grealish, however, had struggled to replicate last season’s form impact when joining He added: “Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, more goals. There’s lots of things about him which we need and he’s good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope The Everton manager has backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place, following after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain
